{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"1a986a441a6cf65b31a5bd4e5f986bc78046a7c58c350a0dde972553bbcbc9c5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Guide signs, pavement markings, signals and roundabouts","heading":"C — Guide signs, pavement markings and traffic signals","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Guide signs, pavement markings and traffic signals

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A53
A roundabout is a circular intersection, usually without a traffic signal, where traffic travels counter-clockwise around a central island. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A53
You enter a roundabout from the right, yielding to vehicles already circulating, and follow the circle to the right until you reach your road. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A53
Guide or informational signs inform and direct drivers, and those giving motorist directions are green and white. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A53
Blue and white guide signs are the ones used for motorist services. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A53
Brown and white guide signs mark points of public recreational or cultural interest. [A53]
Why it matters: blue means services and brown means recreation; the two are easy to swap.
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A54
Mileposts stand along most sections of Alabama's main highways to help drivers pinpoint where they are, to locate emergency incidents, and to aid highway maintenance. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A54
Milepost numbering is meant to start at zero at the south and west state lines, or at the junction where a route begins. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A54
Pavement markings generally come in four types: centerline striping, edge striping, crosswalks and pavement messages. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A54
The centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions, and the manual says it is painted yellow on two-lane highways and white on multi-lane highways and one-way streets. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A54
A broken centerline marks areas with no passing restriction, where you may pass when it is safe. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A54
Where passing is restricted, a solid yellow line runs beside the broken line, and if the solid line is on your side you may not pass. [A54]
Why it matters: the line nearest your lane is the one that governs you.
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A54
When passing is banned for traffic in both directions, the broken line is replaced by two solid yellow lines. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A54
Two or more lanes moving the same way are separated by broken white lines, and you may cross them when passing. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A54
A solid white edge line marks the outside of the traffic lane and may be crossed only by traffic moving onto or off the shoulder. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A54
Yellow left edge lines sometimes appear on divided roads where traffic cannot pull fully off, and yellow also marks obstructions and islands, which you must pass on the right. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A54
A normal solid white line separates lanes going the same direction where crossing is discouraged but not forbidden. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A55
A wide solid white line adds emphasis where crossing calls for unusual care. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A55
A double solid white line separates lanes going the same direction, and crossing it is prohibited. [A55]
Why it matters: a single solid white line discourages crossing, but a double one forbids it.
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A55
Solid white lines mark crosswalks at intersections and sometimes between them, and with no controlling signal a driver must stop at any crosswalk occupied by pedestrians. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A55
Pavement messages such as SCHOOL ZONE or RR CROSSING are painted in white letters on the road to warn of conditions ahead. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A55
On a two-lane, two-way road where passing is banned both ways, you may cross the centerline only as part of a left turn. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A56
On a multi-lane, two-way road, the centerline may be crossed only while making a left turn. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A56
A two-way left turn lane is reserved only for vehicles turning left from either direction. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A56
At a steady circular red light, stop and stay stopped until it turns green, although a right turn, and in certain cases a left turn, is allowed after stopping. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A56
A steady circular yellow follows the green and means clear the intersection; you must not enter once the red comes on. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A56
On a steady circular green you may go straight or turn either way, yielding to vehicles and pedestrians lawfully in the intersection, unless a sign forbids the turn. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A57
Red flashing lights work with crossbuck signs at many railroad crossings, and you must always stop when they begin flashing because a train is near, checking every track before you cross. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A57
Where gates are used with flashing lights, stop as soon as the lights start, before the gates come down, and stay stopped until the gates rise and the lights stop. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0057]

Glossary: guide sign — a sign that informs and directs, colored by its message type [A53]. Centerline — the painted stripe dividing traffic going in opposite directions [A54]. Edge line — the solid line marking the outside edge of the traffic lane [A54].
Memory aid: green goes the way, blue serves, brown plays [A53].
